implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search planner, text/path sources, slice helper, ordering/slicing tests and planning documentation changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, public constructor signature, package version or publication state changed.
implementation.ordering: No ORDER BY is accepted because filesystem directory enumeration is not a portable global ordering contract. Descending, multi-file and tie-sensitive order remains residual for Core.
implementation.slicing: SKIP and TAKE are accepted only when no residual predicate or order remains and both values are non-negative. A shared source-execution window applies after accepted predicate evaluation across all files and path rows; counts still complete each file before output filtering.
implementation.joinSafety: Core can remove an accepted slice only for a direct source plan. The compiled join regression confirms that an unmatched earlier path is not allowed to truncate the join input before the outer TAKE.

scenarios: Fully satisfied accepted predicate and slice are mirrored in the execution plan
Residual predicate or order keeps slice operations residual
Accepted slice is applied after accepted predicate
Accepted TAKE is shared globally across per-file sinks
Residual filter rejects an earlier matching line before TAKE
TAKE after a join does not truncate join inputs

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release suite exited 0 across 21 projects with 1,532 total tests, 1,498 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the Search suite and ordering/slicing-focused tests also passed.

The separate ownership review approved conservative order residuals, global window state, accepted-predicate placement, count completion and direct-join safety; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Focused tests cover residual filtering before TAKE, descending global order, ties, SKIP, TAKE 0, accepted-predicate slicing, cross-file global windows and TAKE after a join.
Accepted SKIP and TAKE are mirrored in both plan containers, applied after accepted predicates by shared source state, and the warnings-as-errors Search build passed.

knownLimitations: Filesystem traversal and content scanning still run to completion even when an accepted TAKE has been reached; TAKE is an output window, not a scan budget.
No global ORDER BY is accepted because traversal order is not a portable ordering guarantee; sorting remains Core residual work.
Residual ordering, grouping, joins and residual predicates keep their slices above the source; the source cannot safely stop those higher-level plans.
The normal search.many planner boundary remains reject-all and its current request-level take options are unchanged.
